assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection into exporting changed how trade is theorized and measured. It shifted the focus from industry-level to firm-level gains, and it generated a large body of empirical work and policy analysis.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central contribution. Helpman's heterogeneous-firm work with Melitz and Yeaple extended it to exporting versus FDI. Redding is a major contributor to quantification, but the core credit is clearest for Melitz and Helpman. Krugman's earlier prize and other predecessors complicate the framing.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of replication, extension and use in applied work. The framework is established and mature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers to pair Helpman with this work or with the political-economy trade work in B001
Whether Redding or other contributors should share credit
How much of the prize-relevant credit is already covered by Krugman's earlier prize

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The credit-cycles model showed how collateral constraints amplify and propagate shocks. It is foundational to macro-finance and to how policy bodies think about financial crises and balance-sheet channels.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore (JPE 1997) is the core paper and is clearly attributable to the two of them. Gertler and Gilchrist belong to the related financial-accelerator empirical and quantitative strand. The 2022 prize recognized related banking and crisis work, which partly overlaps the field.
assessment.maturity: Nearly thirty years of influence, with a strong post-2008 empirical and policy record.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2022 prize for work on banks and financial crises
Whether Gertler should be added, given the Bernanke-Gertler lineage
Extent of direct empirical confirmation of the specific mechanism

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Machine-learning methods for causal inference, including double/debiased ML and heterogeneous-effects estimation, have become standard tools across applied fields. They address high-dimensional controls and treatment-effect heterogeneity with valid inference.
assessment.attribution: Chernozhukov and coauthors on double/debiased ML, and Athey with Wager and Imbens on causal forests and related methods. Credit is spread across a large coauthor network, so the choice of two names is partly arbitrary. Imbens has already been recognized for causal inference.
assessment.maturity: The core work is from roughly 2016 to 2019. Adoption is wide but the technology is still evolving, so it is less mature than the older candidates.
uncertainties: Whether the contribution will be judged as lasting methodology or as a fast-moving toolkit
Credit division among Athey, Wager, Chernozhukov and others
Overlap with the 2021 causal-inference prize

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The intertemporal approach to the current account, the Redux model and the exchange-rate disconnect puzzle shaped modern open-economy macro and the textbook framework used by policy institutions.
assessment.attribution: Obstfeld and Rogoff are the natural pairing through the Foundations text, the Redux model and the disconnect puzzles. Other contributors, such as Sachs, Dornbusch and Svensson, complicate attribution, and the empirical record is mixed on some puzzles.
assessment.maturity: Work from the 1990s with decades of use, though several puzzles remain unresolved.
uncertainties: Some of the central puzzles remain unsolved, which cuts both ways for prize-worthiness
Overlap with B018 for Rogoff, and with Mundell and earlier open-economy prizes
Policy-relevance versus empirical validation

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Law and finance made legal institutions and investor protection a central variable in comparative financial development and corporate governance. The agenda launched a very large literature.
assessment.attribution: La Porta, Lopez-de-Silanes, Shleifer and Vishny (LLSV) share the core papers. Shleifer is also credited for work on behavioral finance and limits to arbitrage. Vishny has a strong claim as a coauthor, but a three-name limit means a choice must be made, which is a weakness.
assessment.maturity: The agenda dates from the late 1990s. Its interpretation has been revisited, and the legal-origins thesis has been challenged on both measurement and causal grounds.
uncertainties: Robustness and replication critiques of the legal-origins results
Limit of three names against four core coauthors
Shleifer's separate reputation and controversies may affect committee views, and I treat them as outside the evidence

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantile regression provides a practical way to study the full conditional distribution rather than only the mean. It is widely used in labour, finance and many applied fields.
assessment.attribution: Koenker and Bassett (1978) is the foundational paper. Chernozhukov is credited for later inference and extensions, but he is better placed under B007 given the three-name limit.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: nearly fifty years of use and extensions.
uncertainties: Whether the contribution is regarded as a tool of broad enough scientific impact for the prize
Whether Chernozhukov should be included instead, given his later extensions
Attribution is clean but the economic discovery content is methodological

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The management-practices work documents large, persistent productivity differences across firms and countries that relate to management quality, and it uses large-scale surveys and field experiments. It connects to the productivity-gap question.
assessment.attribution: Bloom and Van Reenen are the central authors, with Sadun a key long-term coauthor. Bloom also appears in B039 on uncertainty, so a dual-claim issue arises.
assessment.maturity: Roughly twenty years of work. Experimental evidence is useful, but the survey measures and their causal interpretation are still debated.
uncertainties: Measurement and causal interpretation of management scores
Whether the work has changed economic theory or mainly applied empirics
Overlap with Bloom's uncertainty-shock agenda

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative data opened new measurement of intergenerational mobility and neighbourhood effects, with strong policy salience and methodological influence on public and labour economics.
assessment.attribution: Chetty leads the program, with Hendren central to the neighbourhood-effects and mobility work. The group is large, and Friedman and Katz are also important, so credit assignment within a team-based program is hard.
assessment.maturity: Mostly from the 2010s, so relatively recent. Replication and long-run follow-up are still developing.
uncertainties: Relatively short time since the key results
Attribution within a large collaborative program
Causal interpretation of place-based effects and whether the contribution is primarily measurement or theory
